graph.name: coin-cell-led
graph.description: Press the button, the LED lights: a CR2032 coin cell, a push button, a red LED and its series resistor.

purpose.notes: The example of the edakit handbook, chapter 17: built for oneself, a desk gadget for adults, kept out of the reach of small children – the cell comes out by hand (D-5).

components.label: CR2032 holder
components.notes: Pin 1 = plus, pin 2 = minus (datasheet QJ.BS-6). Soldered by hand: JLCPCB places C70377 only under Standard PCBA (D-4) – its ⊕ end (chamfered corner) on pad 1, at the silkscreen '+'.

accept.LIM.i/cell: SW1 is pressed for a moment: while it is held a fresh cell gives up to 10.7 mA, above its 3 mA continuous and below its 15 mA pulse current (Jauch CR 2032 H2B); held longer it costs capacity and voltage, no harm – the voltage drop is in the simulation by the cell's r (D-7)

components.label: LED series resistor
components.notes: R ≤ (2.5 V − 2.27 V) / 1 mA − 40 Ω ≈ 190 Ω for 1 mA from a used cell (2.5 V, 40 Ω) into D1 at its highest Vf; 150 Ω, the value of the block led: 1.2 mA there, 10.7 mA from a fresh cell into D1 at its lowest Vf (sim, D-2)

components.label: LED (red 0805)
components.notes: Red: Vf 1.5–2.6 V at 20 mA – the block's green LED (2.6–3.1 V) stays dark on a used cell (D-2).

nets.name: VBAT
nets.notes: the cell: 3.0 V nominal, 3.2 V and a little more fresh off load; negative with the cell upside down

nets.name: LED_SW
nets.notes: the cell's voltage while SW1 is pressed

accept.PATH.reverse: a cell upside down drives R1 and D1 backwards: D1 blocks, 3.2 V against its VR of 5 V – sim scenario reversed/pressed (LIM.v reverse voltage, SIM.state LED dark); no other part on the board (D-3)

notes: the cell (Ø 20 mm) stands 2 mm out of BT1 (16 mm wide) on both long sides: keep them free, with room to lever the cell out
D1 next to SW1: the LED shows the press

accept.HINT.bulk: no cable and no plug: the cell sits in BT1 on the board, the only load is D1 (at most 11 mA)
accept.HINT.lithium: a CR2032 is a primary Li-MnO2 cell, not Li-ion: nothing on the board charges it (LIM.backfeed) and it is not recharged
